question: Which agent acted?
nist_text_excerpt: AU-3: ... (d) Source of the event; ... (f) Identity of any individuals, subjects, or objects/entities associated with the event. | IA-13: Employ identity providers and authorization servers to manage user, device, and non-person entity (NPE) identities ...
why: AU-3 requires the identity of the subject in the record; an agent is a subject (process, service or non-person entity). This rests on reading an agent as a 'subject', since AU-3(f) is generic.

question: Was the agent's identity verified, and at what level?
nist_controls: IA-9; IA-13; IA-13(2); IA-12(a) (human principal only); AU-10(1)
nist_text_excerpt: IA-9: Uniquely identify and authenticate [system services and applications] before establishing communications ... | IA-13(2): The source and integrity of identity assertions and access tokens are verified before granting access to system and information resources. | IA-12: (a) Identity proof users ... based on appropriate identity assurance level requirements ...
why: Authentication and token verification are required. No control requires the record to state how identity was verified or at what level. IA-12 covers proofing of human users (the principal), not the agent. AU-10(1) binds an information producer to the information; it is not an identity-verification level.

question: On whose behalf did it act?
nist_text_excerpt: IA-2: ... associate that unique identification with processes acting on behalf of those users. | AU-10: Provide irrefutable evidence that an individual (or process acting on behalf of an individual) has performed [actions].
why: IA-2 and IA-8 require the user-to-process association to exist, not to be logged. No control explicitly requires every audit record to name both the acting process and the principal. AU-3(d),(f) and AU-10 come closest; AU-10 applies only to organisation-selected actions and can be met by signatures or receipts rather than log fields. SA-8(22) (accountability and traceability) reaches this only through its guidance. No control statement uses the word 'delegation'; NIST's phrase is 'processes acting on behalf of' users.

question: With which credential or token?
nist_text_excerpt: IA-5: Manage system authenticators by ... (g) Protecting authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification ... | IA-13(2): The source and integrity of identity assertions and access tokens are verified before granting access ...
why: Authenticators must be managed and tokens verified. Recording which credential or token was used for each event is not required. AU-10(3) covers only reviewer or releaser credentials in a chain of custody.

question: Was the action authorised, and under which policy?
link: Direct (outcome, narrow cases) / Indirect (decision and policy)
nist_text_excerpt: AU-3: ... (e) Outcome of the event | AC-6(9): Log the execution of privileged functions. | AC-3(10): Employ an audited override of automated access control mechanisms ... | AC-24: ... to ensure [access control decisions] are applied to each access request prior to access enforcement.
why: Outcome (success or failure) and some narrow events must be logged, but outcome is not evidence of authorisation: an over-privileged agent can succeed. Authorisation decisions must be enforced (AC-3, AC-24); logging the decision and the policy applied is not required unless the organisation adds it (AU-3(1)).

question: Which tool, and which tool version or schema hash?
nist_text_excerpt: CM-8: ... an inventory of system components that ... (5) Includes the following information to achieve system component accountability ... | SR-4: Document, monitor, and maintain valid provenance ... | AU-3: (d) Source of the event
why: Component inventory and provenance are required; the version of the component used is not a required field of each audit record.

question: What action was taken, with what outcome?
nist_text_excerpt: AU-3: (a) What type of event occurred; ... (e) Outcome of the event
why: Directly required content of audit records.

question: Can records be linked across a session or workflow?
link: Direct (time order) / Indirect (session or workflow linkage)
nist_controls: AU-3(b),(c); AU-8; AU-12(1); SC-23(3); AU-14; AU-3(1); AU-16 (cross-organisation only)
nist_text_excerpt: AU-12(1): Compile audit records from [system components] into a system-wide (logical or physical) audit trail that is time-correlated to within [level of tolerance]. | AU-8: (a) Use internal system clocks to generate time stamps for audit records ... | SC-23(3): Generate a unique session identifier for each session ...
why: Time stamps and a time-correlated trail are required; they order records but do not link them to a session or workflow. No statement requires a session, transaction or workflow identifier in audit records ('workflow' appears in no statement). SC-23(3) covers communications-session identifiers only. AU-16 applies only when audit information crosses organisational boundaries.

question: Is the record tamper-evident?
nist_text_excerpt: AU-9: (a) Protect audit information and audit logging tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion; and (b) Alert [personnel or roles] upon detection of unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of audit information. | AU-9(3): Implement cryptographic mechanisms to protect the integrity of audit information ... | AU-7: ... (b) Does not alter the original content or time ordering of audit records.
why: Protection, alerting on modification and (as an enhancement) cryptographic integrity of audit information are required.

question: Who writes the record: the agent itself or an independent component?
nist_text_excerpt: AU-9(2): Store audit records [frequency] in a repository that is part of a physically different system or system component than the system or component being audited. | SC-7(15): Route networked, privileged accesses through a dedicated, managed interface for purposes of access control and auditing. | AU-9(4): Authorize access to management of audit logging functionality to only [subset of privileged users or roles].
why: Separate storage is required (AU-9(2), at an organisation-defined frequency); it controls where records are kept, not who writes them. No control requires the component that generates the record to be independent of the actor whose action is recorded; AU-12(a) places generation on the system components themselves. The nearest related separations are SC-7(15) and AU-9(4).
